perspectives.name: discovery-weak-signals

factors.name: hyperscalerCommittedDemand
factors.basis: Nebius announced a five-year Meta agreement for $12 billion of dedicated AI capacity beginning in early 2027, plus a commitment for Meta to purchase otherwise-unsold capacity from specified upcoming clusters up to $15 billion over five years.

risks: The arrangement requires large-scale capacity buildout and the additional-capacity commitment does not mean all $15 billion will necessarily be purchased.
unknowns: Project-level capital intensity, margins, financing mix and exact capacity ramp remain unknown.

perspectives.name: expectations-execution

factors.name: contractedCapacityExecution
factors.basis: The announced Meta agreement supplies a concrete early-2027 delivery schedule and multi-location demand anchor for Nebius's planned Vera Rubin deployments.

risks: Execution depends on timely construction, equipment deployment and energization of capacity.
unknowns: Revenue recognition cadence and realized utilization outside committed capacity remain unknown.

sources.origin: Nebius Newsroom / Meta AI infrastructure agreement
facts: Five-year agreement provides $12 billion of dedicated capacity to Meta across multiple locations starting early 2027.

Meta also committed to purchase additional available compute capacity across certain upcoming Nebius clusters up to $15 billion over five years, with Nebius intending first to sell that capacity to third parties.

result: Material primary-source contracted-demand evidence packaged for Alpha; financing, margin and numeric underwriting remain Alpha-owned.
